references.text: John the Baptist testified clearly: "I am not the Messiah." This is the same testimony he refers back to in John 1:20, where he openly confessed that he was not the Christ.
In John 1:23, John the Baptist describes his role as "a voice crying out in the wilderness," meaning a forerunner and not the Messiah himself—the same self-understanding he repeats in 3:28.
In John 1:6-8, John is presented as one sent from God to testify about the light, but who was not himself the light. This aligns with his statement of being sent ahead of Christ.
In John 1:15, John testifies that the one coming after him has come before him. This points to the same subordination expressed in 3:28.
In John 1:27, John says he is not worthy to untie the sandal strap of the one coming after him, thereby emphasizing his role as forerunner, not the Messiah.
In Malachi 3:1, a messenger is prophesied who will prepare the way before the Lord. John the Baptist identifies with this role—sent ahead of Christ to make His path straight.
The prophecy in Isaiah 40:3 about a voice crying out in the wilderness and preparing the way for the Lord is the background for John's self-understanding as the one "sent ahead of him."
In John 3:30, John follows up his testimony with the well-known statement: "He must increase, but I must decrease," which is the logical consequence of his being only the forerunner.
In Luke 1:17, the angel says that John will go before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elijah, confirming his role as one sent ahead of Christ.
In Acts 13:25, Paul quotes John's own testimony that he is not the one people think he is, but that someone is coming after him. This confirms the same testimony found in John 3:28.
